harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed inventory-api as a managed systemd service on node1 with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, giving it near-total OOM immunity. Verified that a deliberately unprotected memory-hog process (default oom_score_adj=0) drives the system out of memory and gets selected/killed by the kernel OOM killer, while inventory-api keeps serving reads and writes uninterrupted (same PID throughout, data intact). Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured a boot_id baseline, issued systemctl reboot, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified inventory-api (enabled, active, data intact, OOM protection reapplied on the new PID) recovered, with the mem-hog test service remaining disabled/inert.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (AlmaLinux 9.6, ~1.9GiB RAM, no swap, cgroup v2, systemd-oomd not present)
Built /opt/inventory-api/app.py: stdlib-only HTTP API backed by sqlite at /var/lib/inventory-api/inventory.db (GET /health, GET /inventory, POST /inventory)
Created /etc/systemd/system/inventory-api.service with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 and Restart=always; enabled and started it
Verified the running inventory-api process had live oom_score_adj=-1000
Built /opt/inventory-api/memhog.py and mem-hog.service (default OOM score, never enabled) that allocates memory until the system runs out
Captured pre-disruption baseline: free -m, service active, health/inventory responses
Started mem-hog and polled memory/service state; kernel OOM killer selected and killed the mem-hog PID (confirmed via dmesg oom-kill log) within seconds
Verified inventory-api retained the same PID, stayed active, and served GET/POST requests successfully during and after the OOM event, including writing a new inventory row
Reset-failed and stopped mem-hog; confirmed it was never enabled so it will not return on boot
Captured pre-reboot baseline: boot_id, uptime, service active/enabled, health/inventory data
Issued systemctl reboot on node1 (single node; acknowledgement returned via disconnected exec stream, consistent with a real reboot)
Polled node1 until exec access returned, then confirmed boot_id changed from the pre-reboot value

Verified post-reboot recovery: inventory-api active and enabled with a new PID, oom_score_adj still -1000 (unit-file enforced), all inventory data (including the post-OOM test row) intact, and mem-hog service remained disabled

evidence.requirement: inventory-api runs as a managed (systemd) service
evidence.summary: systemd unit created, enabled, started; service active and responding to /health and /inventory with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 confirmed live on the process
Pre-disruption baseline: free -m, service active, /health ok, /inventory returns seeded data

evidence.requirement: Memory hog drives the system out of memory and is the process the kernel OOM-kills (not inventory-api)
evidence.summary: mem-hog started with default oom_score_adj=0; polling shows free memory collapsing then the hog service failing; dmesg confirms kernel oom-killer selected and killed PID 1438 (python3 mem-hog, oom_score_adj=0), not inventory-api

evidence.requirement: inventory-api keeps serving throughout/after the OOM event, as the protected process
evidence.summary: Post-OOM check: inventory-api still active with unchanged PID 1335, /health ok, GET and POST /inventory both succeed and new data persists
mem-hog confirmed disabled (never enabled), reset-failed and stopped; inventory-api still active and healthy

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: healthy baseline + boot identity before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id=49dafad6-5cc2-457a-b0f6-1219740a651e, uptime, inventory-api active/enabled, health and data all healthy prior to reboot

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: acknowledgement returns before disconnection
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued in background; exec stream closed before completion, consistent with the node going down for reboot

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: changed boot identity proves an actual restart occurred
evidence.summary: Polling attempt failed while node was down (connection reset), then succeeded with boot_id=00bbdee7-55f5-4ca4-88fc-85252a1b3faa — different from the pre-reboot boot_id, and a fresh uptime -s timestamp

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: post-restart recovery of required service and data
evidence.summary: After reboot: inventory-api active with new PID 733, oom_score_adj=-1000 reapplied from unit file, /health ok, /inventory returns all rows including the post-OOM test entry, and mem-hog remains disabled
